```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

Saravanakumar 2026 builds the human PK and receptor-occupancy projection for
TAK-500, an antibody-drug conjugate that links the anti-CCR2 antibody
plozalizumab (TAK-202, MLN1202) to the STING agonist dazostinag (TAK-676). The
paper reports four models, packaged here as four files that share this article:

| Model file | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_cyno` | TAK-500 PK, CCR2 receptor occupancy and monocyte trafficking in cynomolgus monkeys | Equations 1-14, Table 2, Figure 1 |
| `Saravanakumar_2026_plozalizumab_cyno` | Plozalizumab PK in cynomolgus monkeys | Equations 15-18, Table S3, Figure 2 |
| `Saravanakumar_2026_plozalizumab_human` | Plozalizumab PK and unbound CCR2 in healthy adults | Equations 19-25, Table S5, Figure 3 |
| `Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_human` | TAK-500 human projection (human plozalizumab disposition + monkey deconjugation rate) | Methods 'TAK-500 Human PK Projection', Table 3, Figure 4 |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_human"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70522>

All four models hold amounts in nmol and concentrations in nM. Doses in mg are
converted with the antibody molecular weight the paper reports (148,700 g/mol,
so 1 mg = 6.725 nmol and 1 ug/mL = 6.72 nM).

```{r helpers}
mw_ab <- 148700
mg_to_nmol <- function(mg) mg * 1e6 / mw_ab

# Per-subject etas drawn with R's RNG from the model's own OMEGA and passed as
# event-table columns with omega = NA. The cohort is then identical on every
# machine and rxode2 build, so the assertions below test the model, not the
# draw.
draw_etas <- function(omega, n, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * ncol(omega)), n) %*% chol(omega)
  colnames(z) <- colnames(omega)
  as.data.frame(z)
}

# One dose record per subject at time 0 into `cmt` (bolus when dur = 0, else a
# zero-order infusion over `dur` h), then observation records on the same
# state at `times`. `subj` holds id, amt and any per-subject columns. The
# models with several `~` endpoints need `dvid` on observation rows; dvid = 1
# still returns every endpoint column in a forward solve.
build_events <- function(subj, times, cmt = "central", dur = 0) {
  dose <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = cmt, rate = if (dur > 0) amt / dur else 0, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- subj |>
    select(-amt) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = cmt, rate = 0, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

# Assay lower limits of quantification (Methods), in nM: total antibody
# 30 ng/mL and conjugated TAK-676 0.651 ng/mL (LC-MS/MS, MW 148,700 and
# 710.52 g/mol), plozalizumab 0.4 ug/mL (monkey ELISA).
lloq <- c(tab = 30 / 148.7, cp = 0.651 / 710.52 * 1000, ploz_cyno = 0.4 * 6.72)

# PKNCA on one analyte; the dose column is in nmol of the analyte. Samples
# after time zero below `lloq` are dropped, as in the paper's NCA (BQL
# samples are excluded from the terminal phase).
run_nca <- function(sim, conc_col, dose_df, group, dur = 0, end = Inf, lloq = 0) {
  conc <- sim |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    filter(time == 0 | .data[[conc_col]] >= lloq) |>
    transmute(id, time, conc = .data[[conc_col]], group = .data[[group]])
  conc <- bind_rows(
    conc,
    conc |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, group, time)
  dose <- dose_df |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt, group = .data[[group]], duration = dur)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 0, end = end, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
    half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | group + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | group + id, route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}

nca_long <- function(res, group_name) {
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    select(group, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    rename(!!group_name := group)
}
```

# Population

* **Monkey TAK-500 study** (Table 1, Table 2): 12 protein-naive female
  cynomolgus monkeys (2.6-4.5 kg), single IV slow bolus of 0.1, 0.5 or
  3 mg/kg (n = 4 per dose), sampled to 408 h for total antibody and conjugated
  TAK-676 (LC-MS/MS), whole-blood CCR2 receptor occupancy and monocyte counts.
* **Monkey plozalizumab study** (Table S2, Table S3): male and female
  cynomolgus monkeys given a single 30-min IV infusion and sampled to day 36
  (ELISA). The Methods name 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg with 3 males + 3 females per
  dose; the Results and Table S2 describe 1, 3, 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg.
* **Human plozalizumab study** (Table S4, Table S5): phase I single ascending
  dose in healthy volunteers, 1-h IV infusion of 0.1-10 mg/kg, 36 subjects with
  data (6 per dose). Demographics are not reported.
* **TAK-500 human projection** (Table 3, Figure 4): 50, 150 and 500 ug/kg as a
  1-h infusion in a 70 kg adult; no TAK-500 human data were fitted.

The same information is in each model's `population` metadata, e.g.
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_cyno"))$population`.

# TAK-500 in cynomolgus monkeys (Figure 1, Table 1)

The model has no body-weight term: Vc and Vmax are per animal, so a mg/kg dose
has to be multiplied by a weight. Individual weights are not reported, so the
typical animal is solved at the bottom, middle and top of the 2.6-4.5 kg range.

```{r cyno-tak500-sim}
mod_c500 <- readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_cyno")
cyno_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.5), seq(24, 408, by = 4),
                            0.083, 0.83, 6, 72, 168, 240, 336)))
subj_c500 <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose_mgkg = c(0.1, 0.5, 3), WT = c(2.6, 3.55, 4.5)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), amt = mg_to_nmol(dose_mgkg * WT),
         dose = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"), weight = paste(WT, "kg"))
ev_c500 <- build_events(subj_c500, cyno_times)
sim_c500 <- rxSolve(mod_c500, ev_c500, omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                    keep = c("dose", "weight", "WT", "dose_mgkg"),
                    returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 7}
sim_c500 |>
  select(time, dose, weight, `Total antibody (nM)` = Cc_tab,
         `Conjugated payload (nM)` = Cc, `Receptor occupancy (%)` = RO,
         `Monocytes (cells/uL)` = mono) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(time, dose, weight)) |>
  filter(value > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = weight)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(name ~ dose, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Body weight",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1B-M of Saravanakumar 2026 (typical animal).")
```

The shapes follow Figure 1: total antibody and conjugated payload fall
bi-exponentially and faster at lower doses (target-mediated clearance),
receptor occupancy starts near 7% + 59% x C/(5.31 + C) and decays to the 7%
assay background, and monocytes leave the circulation within the first day
and return over 1-2 weeks, more slowly after 3 mg/kg.

```{r cyno-tak500-nca}
dose_c500 <- subj_c500 |> filter(weight == "3.55 kg")
sim_mid <- sim_c500 |> filter(weight == "3.55 kg")
nca_tab <- run_nca(sim_mid, "Cc_tab", dose_c500, "dose", lloq = lloq[["tab"]])
nca_cp <- run_nca(sim_mid, "Cc", dose_c500 |> mutate(amt = 4.6 * amt), "dose", lloq = lloq[["cp"]])

to_cmp <- function(res, analyte) {
  nca_long(res, "dose") |>
    mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs", PPORRES * 1000 / 3.55, PPORRES),
           analyte = analyte)
}
sim_cmp <- bind_rows(to_cmp(nca_tab, "Total Ab"), to_cmp(nca_cp, "Conjugated TAK-676")) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs"))

ref_table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~dose, ~half.life, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~cl.obs,
  "Total Ab", "0.1 mg/kg", 15.4, 14.3, 151, 4.3,
  "Total Ab", "0.5 mg/kg", 58.5, 68, 1273, 2.7,
  "Total Ab", "3 mg/kg", 82.2, 425, 8930, 2.2,
  "Conjugated TAK-676", "0.1 mg/kg", 7.0, 60, 339, 9.2,
  "Conjugated TAK-676", "0.5 mg/kg", 15.7, 295, 3133, 5.0,
  "Conjugated TAK-676", "3 mg/kg", 38.5, 1766, 23239, 3.8
)
cmp_c500 <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_cmp, ref_table1, by = c("analyte", "dose"),
  units = c(cmax = "nM", aucinf.obs = "nM*h", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h/kg")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_c500, caption = paste(
  "Typical 3.55 kg monkey vs. Table 1 means (n = 4 per dose).",
  "* differs by more than 20%."
))
```

```{r cyno-tak500-weight}
wt_tab <- sim_c500 |>
  group_by(dose, weight) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc_tab), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(run_nca(sim_c500 |> mutate(dw = paste(dose, weight)), "Cc_tab",
                          subj_c500 |> mutate(dw = paste(dose, weight)), "dw",
                          lloq = lloq[["tab"]])$result) |>
      filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
      transmute(dose = sub(" [0-9.]+ kg$", "", group), weight = sub("^.* mg/kg ", "", group),
                aucinf = PPORRES),
    by = c("dose", "weight")
  ) |>
  left_join(ref_table1 |> filter(analyte == "Total Ab") |> select(dose, ref_cmax = cmax, ref_auc = aucinf.obs),
            by = "dose") |>
  mutate(cmax_ratio = cmax / ref_cmax, auc_ratio = aucinf / ref_auc)
wt_tab |>
  transmute(Dose = dose, Weight = weight, `Cmax (nM)` = signif(cmax, 3),
            `Cmax / Table 1` = round(cmax_ratio, 2), `AUCinf (nM*h)` = signif(aucinf, 3),
            `AUCinf / Table 1` = round(auc_ratio, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Total-antibody exposure of the typical animal across the reported weight range.")

stopifnot(
  # Structure: the conjugated payload is DAR x ADC, so at the first sample
  # (before appreciable deconjugation) Cc / Cc_tab is close to 4.6, as the
  # Table 1 Cmax ratios (4.2, 4.3, 4.2) show.
  all(abs(with(sim_c500[sim_c500$time == 0.083, ], Cc / Cc_tab) / 4.2 - 1) < 0.15),
  # Table 1 Cmax lies inside the model's weight band (2.6-4.5 kg) at every dose.
  all(tapply(wt_tab$cmax_ratio, wt_tab$dose, min) < 1.15),
  all(tapply(wt_tab$cmax_ratio, wt_tab$dose, max) > 0.85),
  # Known deviation, pinned so a change to the model shows up: the typical
  # animal's AUC is 1.3-3.2 times the Table 1 mean across 2.6-4.5 kg and the
  # three doses (typical-value solve, so the range is deterministic).
  all(wt_tab$auc_ratio > 1.1), all(wt_tab$auc_ratio < 4),
  # Monocytes return towards the 167 cells/uL baseline by 408 h after 0.1 mg/kg.
  all(sim_c500$mono[sim_c500$time == 408 & sim_c500$dose_mgkg == 0.1] > 150)
)
```

Cmax agrees with Table 1 at the light end of the weight range (within 15% at
2.6 kg), but at every weight the typical animal's total-antibody AUC is above
the Table 1 mean (1.3-1.7 times at 2.6 kg, up to 3.2 times at 4.5 kg) and the
clearance is correspondingly lower. The terminal half-life is also longer than
Table 1's at the two lower doses, where the observed concentrations fell below
the assay limit within three days. The packaged values were checked against
Table 2 and its bootstrap medians, which agree. The same gap is visible against
the authors' own Figure 1D curve (about 20 nM at 72 h after 3 mg/kg, versus
about 34-66 nM here). The cause cannot be settled from the publication; see
Assumptions and deviations.

# Plozalizumab in cynomolgus monkeys (Figure 2, Table S2)

```{r cyno-ploz-sim}
mod_cploz <- readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_plozalizumab_cyno")
ui_cploz <- rxode2::rxode(mod_cploz)
n_c <- 200L
doses_cploz <- c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100)
eta_cploz <- draw_etas(ui_cploz$omega, n_c, seed = 2026)
subj_cploz <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose_mgkg = doses_cploz, k = seq_len(n_c)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), WT = 3, amt = mg_to_nmol(dose_mgkg * WT),
         dose = factor(paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"), levels = paste(doses_cploz, "mg/kg"))) |>
  bind_cols(eta_cploz[rep(seq_len(n_c), length(doses_cploz)), , drop = FALSE]) |>
  select(-k)
cploz_times <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24 * c(1:8, 10, 12, 15, 19, 22, 29, 36))
sim_cploz <- rxSolve(mod_cploz, build_events(subj_cploz, cploz_times), omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                     keep = c("dose", "dose_mgkg"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-2}
sim_c500_typ <- sim_c500 |> filter(weight == "3.55 kg", time <= 336)
sim_cploz |>
  filter(dose_mgkg %in% c(0.1, 0.5, 3), time <= 336) |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = sim_c500_typ, aes(time, Cc_tab), colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-3, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (nM)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2C-E of Saravanakumar 2026: plozalizumab 95% PI (blue)",
                       "vs. typical TAK-500 total antibody (red, 3.55 kg)."))
```

Table S2 prints AUC in "h x uM", but its AUC and CL columns agree only if the
AUC is in uM x day (at 100 mg/kg, 672 nmol/kg / 35.2 uM x day = 0.80 mL/h/kg,
against the printed 0.83). The reference values below use uM x day and the
half-lives (printed in days) are converted to hours.

```{r cyno-ploz-nca}
dose_cploz <- subj_cploz |> filter(dose_mgkg >= 1) |> mutate(dose = as.character(dose))
nca_cploz <- run_nca(sim_cploz |> filter(dose_mgkg >= 1) |> mutate(dose = as.character(dose)),
                     "Cc", dose_cploz, "dose", lloq = lloq[["ploz_cyno"]])
sim_cploz_cmp <- nca_long(nca_cploz, "dose") |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs", PPORRES * 1000 / 3, PPORRES))
ref_s2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~aucinf.obs, ~cl.obs, ~half.life,
  "1 mg/kg", 0.167, 1.90, 0.85,
  "3 mg/kg", 1.66, 0.53, 2.0,
  "10 mg/kg", 5.43, 0.66, 3.7,
  "30 mg/kg", 15.8, 0.59, 2.3,
  "100 mg/kg", 35.2, 0.83, 4.3
) |>
  mutate(aucinf.obs = aucinf.obs * 24000, half.life = half.life * 24)
cmp_cploz <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_cploz_cmp, ref_s2, by = "dose",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "nM*h", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h/kg")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_cploz, caption = paste(
  "Median of 200 simulated monkeys per dose vs. Table S2 means (n = 3).",
  "* differs by more than 20%."
))
```

The plozalizumab model reproduces clearance within 35% at 1, 10, 30 and
100 mg/kg. Table S2's 3 mg/kg mean clearance (0.53 mL/h/kg, n = 3) is lower
than its 10-100 mg/kg means, which a model with saturable elimination cannot
reproduce; with three animals per dose and a kel variance of 0.88 such
scatter in the means is expected. In Figure 2
the authors overlay this model on the TAK-500 total-antibody data; the packaged
TAK-500 typical curve sits inside the plozalizumab interval, as in the paper.

```{r cyno-ploz-check}
cl_cploz <- sim_cploz_cmp |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs") |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(cl = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ref_s2 |> select(dose, ref = cl.obs), by = "dose")
cl_cploz_ok <- cl_cploz |> filter(dose != "3 mg/kg")
stopifnot(
  # Nonlinearity: median clearance at 1 mg/kg is well above that at 100 mg/kg.
  with(cl_cploz, cl[dose == "1 mg/kg"] / cl[dose == "100 mg/kg"]) > 1.5,
  # Within 35% of the Table S2 means at 1, 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg. The 3 mg/kg
  # mean (0.53 mL/h/kg) is below the 10-100 mg/kg means, which no saturable
  # model can produce, and is excluded.
  all(abs(cl_cploz_ok$cl / cl_cploz_ok$ref - 1) < 0.35)
)
```

# Plozalizumab in healthy adults (Figure 3, Table S4)

```{r human-ploz-sim}
mod_hploz <- readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_plozalizumab_human")
ui_hploz <- rxode2::rxode(mod_hploz)
n_h <- 100L
doses_h <- c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 6, 10)
eta_h <- draw_etas(ui_hploz$omega, n_h, seed = 202)
subj_h <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose_mgkg = doses_h, k = seq_len(n_h)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), amt = mg_to_nmol(dose_mgkg * 70),
         dose = factor(paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"), levels = paste(doses_h, "mg/kg"))) |>
  bind_cols(eta_h[rep(seq_len(n_h), length(doses_h)), , drop = FALSE]) |>
  select(-k)
h_times <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168, 240, 336, 504, 672,
             1008, 1344, 1680, 2016, 2688)
sim_hploz <- rxSolve(mod_hploz, build_events(subj_h, h_times, dur = 1), omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                     keep = c("dose", "dose_mgkg"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r human-ploz-nca}
dose_h <- subj_h |> mutate(dose = as.character(dose))
nca_h <- run_nca(sim_hploz |> mutate(dose = as.character(dose)), "Cc", dose_h, "dose", dur = 1)
sim_h_cmp <- nca_long(nca_h, "dose") |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs", PPORRES * 1000 / 70, PPORRES))
ref_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~cl.obs, ~half.life,
  "0.1 mg/kg", 15.5, 0.613, 1.19, 1.4,
  "0.3 mg/kg", 49.7, 2.81, 0.758, 2.2,
  "1 mg/kg", 168, 21.7, 0.325, 5.2,
  "3 mg/kg", 529, 96.7, 0.221, 7.1,
  "6 mg/kg", 1266, 252, 0.179, 8.3,
  "10 mg/kg", 1965, 575, 0.125, 9.5
) |>
  mutate(aucinf.obs = aucinf.obs * 1000, half.life = half.life * 24)
cmp_h <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_h_cmp, ref_s4, by = "dose",
  units = c(cmax = "nM", aucinf.obs = "nM*h", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h/kg")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_h, caption = paste(
  "Median of 100 simulated 70 kg adults per dose vs. Table S4 means (n = 6).",
  "* differs by more than 20%."
))

cl_h <- sim_h_cmp |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs") |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(cl = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ref_s4 |> select(dose, ref = cl.obs), by = "dose")
cl_h_hi <- cl_h |> filter(dose %in% c("1 mg/kg", "3 mg/kg", "6 mg/kg", "10 mg/kg"))
stopifnot(
  # Clearance falls with dose (Table S4: 1.19 -> 0.125 mL/h/kg).
  with(cl_h, cl[dose == "0.1 mg/kg"] / cl[dose == "10 mg/kg"]) > 2.5,
  # Within 35% of Table S4 from 1 to 10 mg/kg.
  all(abs(cl_h_hi$cl / cl_h_hi$ref - 1) < 0.35)
)
```

From 1 to 10 mg/kg the simulated clearance is within 30% of Table S4. At 0.1
and 0.3 mg/kg the model's clearance is about half the NCA value. This gap
belongs to the paper's model, not to the transcription: the same parameters
give the authors' own Table 3 clearance of 40 mL/h (0.57 mL/h/kg) at
50 ug/kg, which the packaged projection reproduces below. The NCA half-lives
at low doses were estimated from samples that fell below the assay limit
within a few days, and the paper's half-lives at high doses come from the
saturated phase; the simulated terminal phase is the low-concentration,
target-mediated one, so half-lives are not comparable.

Unbound CCR2 drops at once to about RO0 x (1 - 0.522 C / (5.71 + C)), stays
suppressed while plozalizumab is above a few nM, and climbs back to the
21,509 MESF baseline as the antibody clears, later after higher doses, as in
Figure 3I-N.

# TAK-500 human projection (Figure 4, Table 3)

```{r human-tak500-sim}
mod_h500 <- readModelDb("Saravanakumar_2026_tak_500_human")
ui_h500 <- rxode2::rxode(mod_h500)
n_p <- 200L
doses_p <- c(50, 150, 500)
p_times <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168, 216, 264, 336)
make_proj <- function(eta) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(dose_ugkg = doses_p, k = seq_len(n_p)) |>
    mutate(id = row_number(), amt = mg_to_nmol(dose_ugkg * 70 / 1000),
           dose = paste(dose_ugkg, "ug/kg")) |>
    bind_cols(eta[rep(seq_len(n_p), length(doses_p)), , drop = FALSE]) |>
    select(-k)
}
subj_p <- make_proj(draw_etas(ui_h500$omega, n_p, seed = 500))
sim_p <- rxSolve(mod_h500, build_events(subj_p, p_times, dur = 1), omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                 keep = c("dose", "dose_ugkg"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

The projection reproduces Table 3: clearance of total antibody falls from
about 40 to 31 mL/h between 50 and 500 ug/kg and conjugated-payload clearance
from about 148 to 124 mL/h, with matching 95% intervals. The median
conjugated-payload half-life depends on which phase the terminal fit
selects once concentrations drop below the 0.92 nM assay limit; the simulated
medians lie inside Table 3's 95% intervals at all three doses but do not
match its medians. The simulated Cmax
here is the individual prediction; Table 3's Cmax medians run about 9% higher
and its intervals are wider, consistent with the authors' simulations
including the 16% proportional residual error.

## How the IIV column is read

The supplement's 'eta' column (e.g. 25 on kel, 60 on Km, 21 for the Km-kel
covariance) does not say whether it is a variance x 100 (Phoenix reports Omega
as variances) or a %CV. Table 3's intervals decide it. Under the %CV reading
the Vc variance would be log(1 + 0.02^2) = 0.0004, which makes the total
antibody Cmax nearly identical across subjects; Table 3's Cmax interval spans a
factor of two.

```{r iiv-reading}
om_cv <- ui_h500$omega
cv <- c(etalvc = 0.02, etalkel = 0.25, etalkm = 0.60, etalrbase = 0.02, etalimax = 0.04)
diag(om_cv)[names(cv)] <- log(1 + cv^2)
om_cv["etalkel", "etalkm"] <- om_cv["etalkm", "etalkel"] <-
  0.21 * sqrt(om_cv["etalkel", "etalkel"] * om_cv["etalkm", "etalkm"])
om_cv["etalrbase", "etalimax"] <- om_cv["etalimax", "etalrbase"] <-
  0.02 * sqrt(om_cv["etalrbase", "etalrbase"] * om_cv["etalimax", "etalimax"])
subj_cv <- make_proj(draw_etas(om_cv, n_p, seed = 500))
sim_cv <- rxSolve(mod_h500, build_events(subj_cv, p_times, dur = 1), omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                  keep = c("dose"), returnType = "data.frame")
width <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    group_by(dose, id) |>
    summarise(cmax = max(Cc_tab), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(dose) |>
    summarise(ratio = quantile(cmax, 0.975) / quantile(cmax, 0.025), .groups = "drop")
}
iiv_cmp <- width(sim_p) |>
  rename(`Variance x 100 (packaged)` = ratio) |>
  left_join(width(sim_cv) |> rename(`%CV` = ratio), by = "dose") |>
  mutate(`Table 3` = c(`50 ug/kg` = 11.4 / 5.4, `150 ug/kg` = 34.6 / 16.7,
                       `500 ug/kg` = 115.7 / 56.8)[dose])
knitr::kable(iiv_cmp, digits = 2,
             caption = "97.5th / 2.5th percentile ratio of total-antibody Cmax under the two readings.")

cl_pi <- pi_p |> filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs")
thalf_cp <- pi_p |> filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", analyte == "Conjugated TAK-676")
stopifnot(
  # Conjugated-payload half-life: simulated median inside Table 3's 95% CI.
  all(thalf_cp$med > thalf_cp$ref_lo & thalf_cp$med < thalf_cp$ref_hi),
  # The packaged (variance) reading spreads Cmax by a factor near 1.8 (Table 3:
  # 2.0-2.1 with residual error included); the %CV reading by under 1.15.
  all(iiv_cmp$`Variance x 100 (packaged)` > 1.5),
  all(iiv_cmp$`%CV` < 1.15),
  # Central tendency of clearance matches Table 3 for both analytes.
  all(abs(cl_pi$med / cl_pi$ref_med - 1) < 0.15),
  # The 95% interval of clearance matches Table 3 (both ends within 30%).
  all(abs(cl_pi$lo / cl_pi$ref_lo - 1) < 0.3),
  all(abs(cl_pi$hi / cl_pi$ref_hi - 1) < 0.3)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** The 'eta' columns of Table 2, Table S3 and Table S5 are read
  as the Phoenix Omega variance x 100 (kel 25 -> 0.25). This reading
  reproduces Table 3's 95% intervals of clearance and Cmax; the %CV reading
  gives intervals far too narrow (see "How the IIV column is read"). The two
  printed covariances ('omega Km,Kel' 21, 'omega ROb,Emax' 2) are read on the
  same scale (correlations 0.54 and 0.71).
* **Monkey TAK-500 exposure.** At every weight in the reported 2.6-4.5 kg
  range the typical-animal total-antibody AUC exceeds the Table 1 mean (about
  1.2-1.6 times at 2.6 kg, more at higher weights), and the typical curve sits
  above the authors' Figure 1 simulation after the first day. Table 2 was
  checked against its own bootstrap medians, which agree with the point
  estimates. No parameter was adjusted; the gap is recorded as a known
  deviation and pinned in the assertions above.
* **Monkey weights.** Table 2 Vc and Vmax are per animal and individual weights
  are not reported, so monkey simulations show 2.6, 3.55 and 4.5 kg.
* **Peripheral monocytes at baseline.** Equations 11-12 do not state an
  initial value for the peripheral monocyte pool. It starts at 0, so that
  monocytes leave the circulation only under drug-induced occupancy and return
  to the 167 cells/uL baseline after washout, as in Figure 1K-M.
* **Equation 9 notation.** Equation 9 writes the occupancy denominator as
  'Km + s2'; the parameter is the EC50 of Table 2 (5.31 nM), not the PK Km.
* **Plozalizumab monkey parameters per kg.** Table S3 gives Vc in L/kg and
  Vmax in nmol/h/kg (Table S1 prints the Vmax unit as nmol/h). The per-kg
  reading is used and implemented as a linear WT scaling, so concentrations
  do not depend on the weight supplied. The infusion (30 min) is modelled as
  an IV bolus, as in the paper's model. Table S2 AUC is taken as uM x day (see
  above). The Methods and the Results disagree on the monkey dose levels.
* **Human weight.** The human models carry no weight covariate; simulations
  use 70 kg, the standard of Table 3. The Table S4 comparison is therefore for a
  70 kg subject against the observed cohort means.
* **Emax unit.** Table S5 prints the Emax unit as 1/h; Equation 22 makes it a
  fraction, which is how it is used. Bootstrap medians differ slightly from the
  point estimates (Emax 0.539, IC50 6.50 nM, Vmax 1.69 nmol/h); the point
  estimates are used.
* **Projection DAR.** The Methods use a mean DAR of 4.6; the Figure 4 caption
  says the projections are for DAR 4. Table 3's conjugated-payload Cmax
  (34, 101, 339 nM) equals 4.6 times the typical total-antibody concentration
  at the end of the infusion, so 4.6 is used.
* **Projection residual error and RO.** The projection carries the
  plozalizumab residual errors (16% on concentrations, assumed also for the
  conjugated payload; 23% on unbound CCR2). Receptor occupancy in Figure 4B is
  the human Equation 22 driven by total antibody, expressed as
  100 x (1 - unbound / baseline).
* **kdec.** The human projection uses the monkey estimate 0.0324 1/h (Table 2);
  the Results text rounds it to 0.03 1/h.
* No erratum or correction notice for this article was found (checked
  2026-11-12).
